name: marmot-e1b780ee-blind30-ots
instr:
# marmot-regen

People sign in to this thing, feed descriptions of their company's data into it, look those descriptions up again, and drive the whole lot from a terminal or from a cluster. A pile of unrelated regressions has surfaced since the last round of edits landed. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. Everything below is what we managed to reproduce from the outside, in the order we hit it.

Getting in is the worst of it. Somebody we have never seen before presents a signed identity document minted by an outside issuer, and the sign-in fails outright instead of creating their account and handing it back. The browser handshake that ends in a one-time code dead-ends too: registering an application, being bounced to the sign-in page, and getting a code and the original state value back all still work, but presenting that code to obtain an access pass comes back a failure rather than a pass of the expected kind. The periodic sweep meant to throw away pending one-time codes past their expiry also throws away codes still well inside their lifetime. Past sign-in, what somebody may do has gone slack: a member who may read and write catalogued items is now also allowed to remove them, because the check passes when only the kind of object matches, or only the action matches, instead of requiring both.
